1. Enable "USB debugging" and connect your phone to the computer with a cable.
2. Tap "View command", then send it to the PC or copy it.
3. Paste the command into a terminal on the computer: it will start the server over ADB.

Wi-Fi pairing is not needed for this. You can unplug the cable after starting.

1. Enable "Wireless debugging" — the button below opens the settings.
2. Tap "Pair device with code": the system will show a port and a code.
3. Without closing the settings, pull down the shade and enter the port and code in the Foxhole notification.

Foxhole will pair and offer to open the app — the server will start on its own.
The code is valid for about 2 minutes.

About PCs: `adb pair` gives the key to the computer, not to Foxhole — auto-start needs Foxhole's own key, so the step above is required.

Important: Wi-Fi pairing works only on Android 11 (API 30) and newer. On older versions use "Start from a PC".
While the code window is open (cable or split screen)
The pairing port stays open only while the code window is on screen — for example, if you put Foxhole back into split screen with the settings.
Not available on this Android version
Any shell commands as shell (uid 2000). The hint under the field explains what you type. Command history is stored only on the phone and shown with secrets masked.
Access requests, levels and the list of installed apps. Works through the server.
Package selection, the \"Uninstalled\" bin, restore. Works through the server.

Android allows running commands as shell (uid 2000) via ADB — that is not root (uid 0), but it is enough for pm, appops, settings, dumpsys and any shell commands.\n\nFoxhole starts a Java process through app_process as shell and talks to it over localhost with a token. Third-party apps go through the com.sitikplay.foxhole.bridge ContentProvider and get access only after your approval.

1. Settings → Developer options → "Wireless debugging".
2. Open "Pair device with pairing code": it shows the IP, port and code.
3. Without closing the settings, open the shade, expand the Foxhole notification, tap "Enter port and code" and enter the port and code.

From a PC, instead of step 3:
adb pair <IP>:<pairing port> <code>
adb connect <IP>:<debug port>

The pairing port is the one from the code window. The debug port is from the
"Wireless debugging" screen. The code lives for about 2 minutes.

1. Enable "USB debugging" and connect the phone with a cable.
2. Check that the computer sees the device:
adb devices
3. In Foxhole tap "View command" and copy it.
4. Run the command in a terminal on the PC:
adb shell sh "/storage/emulated/0/Android/data/com.sitikplay.foxhole/files/start.sh"

The server lives until the phone reboots or Foxhole is force-stopped. Wi-Fi pairing is not needed.
To bring the server back after a reboot, repeat step 4.
Ready-made adb pair and adb connect — for pairing from a computer. The IP and port are in the \"Pair device with code\" window; take the code from the same place.
Permissions are tied to the uid — they cannot be spoofed. An app lands in the pending list the first time it asks for access.
You can approve an app in advance — no need to wait for its request.

Usually the APK is copied to the \"Uninstalled\" bin. Irreversible: for user apps no copy is kept (it can only be re-downloaded), for system apps no record is created (but the app physically stays hidden in the system).

After a reboot Foxhole will enable wireless debugging by itself, connect with the paired key and start the server. Requires Android 11+, Wi-Fi, \"Start without a PC\" pairing and a working server for the permission grant. After \"Stop\", autostart will kick in only after the next reboot.\n\nMIUI/HyperOS may block background starts — autostart will not work there.
WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission: not granted (needed to enable debugging)
Debugging is turned off only if autostart enabled it itself; your manual enabling is left alone.

Wi-Fi pairing is unavailable: Android 11+ is required.

PC pairing does not replace this step: the PC key works for the computer only. After a reboot the phone connects with Foxhole\'s key, which appears after \"Start without a PC\" → \"Pair\" (port and code from the \"Pair device with code\" window — once is enough).
Could not grant the permission: start the server and try again
On Android %1$s Wi-Fi pairing is unavailable: Android 11+ is required. Use \"Start from a PC\".

A working server is required. You can pick any package — there is no protective list.

User apps (pm uninstall): the APK is copied to the bin for %1$d days in advance, from there the app can be brought back — data is not restored though.

System apps (pm uninstall -k --user 0): the app physically stays in the system partition, no space is freed — it is simply hidden from you. It can be returned at any moment on the "Restore" tab.

APKs of user apps are kept for %1$d days, then removed automatically: the \"Restore\" button disappears. A hidden system app stays in the system — after that term it can only be brought back with the command pm install-existing --user 0 <package>.\n\nRestore brings back only the app, WITHOUT data.
